## Prose form

([why](rationale.md#prose-form))

Long-lived prose on this project follows one basic shape: a short intro that explains the *why* or
the high-level *what*, sharpened to a *problem statement* where a surface calls for one (see
[Problem-first shape](#problem-first-shape)), then a `-` bullet list for the details. The width
numbers and the wrap discipline live in [Line widths](#line-widths) below, their one home. One fact
per bullet or sub-bullet beats a paragraph packing several. Avoid wall-of-prose paragraphs: they
hide the structure that bullets make scannable. Punctuation that joins clauses without naming their
relationship is the same failure at sentence scale. See [Semicolons](#semicolons) and [Typeable
punctuation only](#typeable-punctuation-only).

Surfaces that use this shape:

- Module / function / struct / field doc comments in `.rs` files. See [Doc
  comments](code.md#doc-comments-on-every-file-function-and-method).
- Commit message bodies (both work-repo and agent-repo). The title is the commit-specific add-on.
  See [The per-rung flow](../AGENTS.md#the-per-rung-flow).
- The cycle-record, `TODO.md > ## In Progress`. See [The In Progress
  block](notes.md#the-in-progress-block).
- Todo entries in `TODO.md` when an entry needs more than one line of detail. Pure one-liners are
  still fine.

Bullet *content* differs by surface:

- **Commit bodies**: the [Problem-first shape](#problem-first-shape) for finished work, as two
  paragraphs by [Commit-body form](#commit-body-form) below. What is specific to a commit:
  - the problem statement defines any word the title assumes, since the title is what a reader meets
    first and it answers the problem
  - **no file list.** The diff and `git show --stat` are the mechanical record, so restating them is
    a second copy that can drift from the first. An import of a thousand files is one change
  - these are claims a reader has to follow, so they are sentences rather than fragments. What
    wants more than a paragraph belongs in the cycle-record instead
  - the **deliberation** stays out: alternatives weighed, evidence, dates, costs accepted. Those
    live in the cycle-record, the `## Todo` entry, and the session the `ochid:` trailer names, each
    reachable from the commit by construction. The problem itself is a *why* and belongs here
- **Cycle-record / todo**: bullets are conceptual (design points, structural notes, the "what landed
  and why" at a notch above file-list granularity). Never a copy of the commit's edit list. The diff
  is the mechanical record, the commit body the problem and solution, the cycle-record the design
  thinking, and none restates another.
- **Doc comments**: bullets are whatever structure fits (fields, cases, invariants).

### Leads are labels, unmarked

In a list item or a numbered step, a lead is a short label ending in a colon, with no markup, and
the sentence after it is complete without it:

```
1. Backfill: fill every as-built ladder whose commits have landed, before anything else.
```

- Label names, sentence instructs: a reader's eye takes bold at the head of an item as the item's
  name and resumes at the plain text expecting a full sentence, so a bold lead that is the
  sentence's own verb or subject (`**Backfill** every as-built ladder ...`) loses its imperative to
  the reader who skips it. Measured 2026-08-21, at the review of the rule that example is from: the
  reviewer read "every as-built ladder" and stopped, with nothing telling them what to do.
- The inverted case: a rule stated in bold is the same failure inverted. When the bold is a whole
  sentence and the plain text is commentary, the reader who skips bold reads the commentary as the
  rule. The fix is the same: a short name as the label, the rule as the plain sentence. The hard
  rules in AGENTS.md are the instance, and the names they gained are greppable and survive a
  renumbering.
- Definitions: the same shape, `Term: what it means.` A period after a bold term (`**Term.** ...`)
  reads as a heading, which is the label reading again.
- No markup on the label: bold is what makes the eye treat the lead as a heading and skip it, and
  the agent-files are read by an agent, which needs no emphasis. The colon alone marks the label
  (wink, 2026-08-21).
- The price: one word of redundancy, paid on purpose: the label is skippable, the sentence is not.

### One spelling per term

A defined term has one spelling, everywhere: `work-repo` and `agent-repo` are always hyphenated,
`agent-files`, `version-of-record`, `dual-repo`, and `as-built` likewise, and no rule varies the
spelling by how the term is used. Terminology in AGENTS.md defines the terms, and this section is
where the spelling rule lives, since a glossary is read for meaning rather than for spelling.

### Bullet form

A bullet is a full sentence, capitalized and ending in a period or question mark, unless the list
is a plain list of things (files, names, options), which takes neither. A list is all one or all
the other. A sentence never opens with a lower-case name (`squash-push`, `rationale.md`), it is
recast so the name is not the first word.

### Line widths

Every width number lives here and nowhere else: the other files and sections link here rather than
restating one, so a change is a single edit and the copies cannot drift. Consolidated 2026-08-09,
when the body width moved and the restatements had to be hunted.

- **Prose**, all durable text: wrap at <=100 cols, bullet continuations indented two spaces.
- **Source**, doc comments and inline comments included: <=100 cols, which is rustfmt's default
  `max_width` (enforcement notes in [code.md](code.md#line-width)).
- **Commit titles**: <=50 chars.
- **Commit bodies**: <=75 cols, the Linux kernel patch standard. It replaced git's older 72
  convention here 2026-08-09, and published bodies keep the wrap they shipped with.

The widths are wrap defaults, not absolutes (the title cap excepted). Existing text re-wraps when
touched, no mass sweeps. Write to the full width: wrap near the limit rather than imitating the
narrow wrap of older text, and a line that reads better long stays long (an URL, a literal report
row, indented code in a comment).

### Problem-first shape

`## In Progress` cycle blocks, `## Todo` entries, and commit bodies use a sharper form of the same
shape: a problem, then how it is answered, then the steps that get there.

- **Problem statement** (the why): one or two sentences. Don't pad with intent, don't restate what
  follows it.
- **Solution statement** (the what/how): what is done about the problem, in broad terms, answering
  whatever question the problem statement raises. Surface-specific rules are in [Bullet content
  differs by surface](#prose-form) above.
- **Plan bullets** (the what/when), the steps. Formality differs by surface:
  - In Progress: a committed ladder, one step per commit. See [Conventional-commit
    shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit) for the per-step title + `(current)` /
    `(done)` form.
  - Todo entries: rough informal bullets, no numbering, formalized only when the entry is picked up
    into a cycle.

**Timing decides whether the solution statement is provisional, not whether it is written.** A cycle
writes one at Preparation, before the work, and revises it as steps land. The close-out's commit
body carries the final one. A `## Todo` entry's is provisional in the same way. Only a commit body's
is settled, because a commit is finished by the time it has one. The earlier rule here said a plan
was for work not yet done and a solution for work that is, which left a cycle unable to say at its
opening what it intended to do.

154	### Semicolons
155	
156	Prose carries no semicolons. A semicolon appears only in code (code spans, fenced code, source
157	files), where it is syntax rather than prose. The structure a semicolon would have joined is written
158	explicitly instead:
159	
160	- **Two claims** take a period, each half standing as its own sentence ("The diff empties. The
161	  history keeps the record.").
162	- **A continuation** takes a comma with a conjunction, when one half carries the other's thought
163	  onward rather than making its own claim.
164	- **A list hiding in prose** (`A; B; C` inside a sentence or bullet) breaks into sub-bullets so the
165	  structure shows. List items that themselves contain commas restructure the same way rather than
166	  separating with semicolons.
167	
168	The code allowance is why a bare byte scan cannot enforce the rule: a checker blanks the code first,
169	then expects zero.
170	
171	The agent-files (`AGENTS.md`, `agent-data/*`) carry no historical exemption and are swept
172	to zero. Any other historical file keeps its existing semicolons only until it is touched: a commit
173	that edits a file makes that whole file's prose semicolons owed, code spans exempt, and the cycle
174	pays them in a penultimate rung of its own, or in its one commit when single-step, using the joins
175	above, so the touching rung's diff reads as its change alone. What is owed still follows from
176	touching the file, and only the payment moves. New prose is written correct and is never a sweep
177	item. A file whose count means rewriting rather than repunctuating becomes its own cycle. Files
178	outside a cycle's diff are never converted, since that is a sweep and sweeps are their own cycle.
179	Source-file comments are prose under this rule (see [code.md](code.md#comments-are-prose)).
180	
181	### Typeable punctuation only
182	
183	Durable text uses punctuation that can be typed at a terminal. The prohibition is on *authoring*,
184	not presence: a file may legitimately hold a banned character it transcribed (see below), so a byte
185	scan is not the rule and a sweep needs the authored/transcribed judgment. Banned from authoring:
186	`—`, `–`, `…`, `→`. None can be entered without a compose key or a paste, so none can be grepped
187	for, and an em dash next to option syntax reads as another flag. Like the semicolon rule above, the
188	agent-files are swept to zero and any other file converts whole when a cycle touches it, paid in
189	the same penultimate rung as the semicolons (specimens and transcriptions aside, below). A banned
190	character costs nothing to write and is paid on every read, so the rule is not softer than that.
191	
192	`…` becomes `...` and `→` becomes `->`. The dashes have no single replacement, because an em dash
193	usually stands in for a structural decision that was not made. Make the decision:
194	
195	- **A bullet's title and its body sharing a line** is a heading and a paragraph. Make the body
196	  sub-bullets.
197	- **A term and its definition** (`jj diff`, `<base>`, a flag) takes a colon, which keeps a glossary
198	  or a command list at one line per entry.
199	- **A prose aside** takes a comma, parentheses, or two sentences. Often the aside should just go.
200	
201	Converting a heading moves its anchor. The em dash strips but the spaces on both sides survive, so
202	`## A — B` slugs to `#a--b` while its colon form slugs to `#a-b` (see [Markdown anchor
203	links](notes.md#markdown-anchor-links)). Re-point inbound links in the same commit.
204	
205	Scope is the same as [Speculation marker](#speculation-marker), plus commit titles and everything
206	under `src/`: doc comments, inline comments, and any user-visible string. Source is the surface a
207	human edits and greps most, so an untypeable character costs more there than in prose. A code span
208	is not exempt by itself. Naming the character is a specimen and stays, which is how this section
209	names them. A banned character doing a job is a use and converts: `` `.expect(…)` `` becomes
210	`` `.expect(...)` ``.
211	
212	Text quoted from outside this repo's prose (tool output, an error message, an already-published
213	commit title) is transcribed, not written, so it keeps its characters, whether or not it sits in a
214	code span. It matters most for commit titles: converting one stops it matching `git log --grep` and
215	breaks the verbatim identity that [Conventional-commit
216	shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit) requires between a commit title and its ladder
217	rung.
218	
219	### Conventional-commit shape (ladder / commit)
220	
221	([why](rationale.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit))
222	
223	A ladder step and its commit description share a *title* shape, a [Conventional
224	Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) title (`<type>: <desc>`, an optional
225	`(scope)` after the type: `feat(push): ...`) over [Prose form](#prose-form) detail. They differ in
226	the title's marker (below) and in bullet *content*: commit bodies take the [Commit-body
227	form](#commit-body-form), the ladder's are conceptual (see "Bullet *content* differs by surface"
228	above). The shared template:
229	
230	```
231	<title>                          # <title> is the commit's `<type>: <desc>`
232	<optional prose intro>
233	  - <optional item>
234	    <optional prose intro>
235	      - <optional sub-item>
236	      ...
237	```
238	
239	The two surfaces apply it as:
240	
241	- **Ladder step** (`zTOC.md` `## Ladder`): the rung is `- N (marker) [<title>](TODO.md#<slug>)`: its
242	  version suffix, the `(current)` / `(done)` marker, and the title linked to the rung's subsection
243	  in `TODO.md` (the closing rung linked like the rest). Its position in the list is its position in
244	  the ladder. The last rung is the close-out and its text says so. Detail lives not on the rung but
245	  in its subsection under `TODO.md`'s `#### Rungs`, headed by the rung's exact title (see the
246	  protocol's [Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)), bulleted, never `;`-joined inline.
247	- **Commit description**: no prefix. The title is the first line, and the body is the prose (see
248	  [Commit description](../AGENTS.md#commit-description)).
249	
250	The title is **identical** across both for a given step, so a step's ladder entry and its commit
251	title line up verbatim. The rung's subsection heading carries the same title, a third
252	surface on every rung (the closing rung's exists only when close-out gotchas occurred: see the
253	protocol's [Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)). Pick the commit title first and reuse it.
254	
255	That identity is **per step**, not per cycle: each step in a cycle gets its own distinct descriptive
256	title, never one shared cycle title uniquified by a step marker. The block's title heading carries
257	the *cycle title*, the bare name no multi-step commit carries (see the bookends below). To keep a
258	cycle's commits collectable with one `git log --grep`, give the step titles a common greppable stem
259	(e.g. `config loader`).
260	
261	**Cycle bookend titles**: a multi-step cycle's bookend commits are the cycle title plus a suffix, "
262	opening" and " closing", or " dead-end closing" for a dead end, whose suffix the title cap does not
263	bind, same type (`feat: dynamic warmup opening` / `feat: dynamic warmup closing`), so one `git log
264	--grep "<cycle title>"` returns the pair that brackets the ladder. The bare cycle title is the
265	cycle's *name*: the block's title heading carries it, and no multi-step commit does, which is also
266	what keeps the closing rung's subsection anchor clear of the title heading's. A single-step cycle's
267	one commit is the cycle and keeps the bare title, in both repos and in its one ladder rung ([Cycle
268	shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)). The type repeats across the pair even though the bookends are
269	mostly bookkeeping: identical prefixes make them scannable. Rungs between keep their own titles on
270	the stem.
271	
272	### Commit titles and descriptions

the title's marker (below) and in bullet *content*: commit bodies take the [Commit-body
form](#commit-body-form), the ladder's are conceptual (see "Bullet *content* differs by surface"
above). The shared template:

```

<optional prose intro>
  - <optional item>

      - <optional sub-item>
      ...

  the ladder. The last rung is the close-out and its text says so. Detail lives not on the rung but

title line up verbatim. The rung's subsection heading carries the same title, a third
surface on every rung (the closing rung's exists only when close-out gotchas occurred: see the
protocol's [Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)). Pick the commit title first and reuse it.

opening" and " closing", or " dead-end closing" for a dead end, whose suffix the title cap does not
bind, same type (`feat: dynamic warmup opening` / `feat: dynamic warmup closing`), so one `git log

cycle's *name*: the block's title heading carries it, and no multi-step commit does, which is also
what keeps the closing rung's subsection anchor clear of the title heading's. A single-step cycle's
one commit is the cycle and keeps the bare title, in both repos and in its one ladder rung ([Cycle
shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)). The type repeats across the pair even though the bookends are
mostly bookkeeping: identical prefixes make them scannable. Rungs between keep their own titles on
the stem.

# Code conventions

Conventions for source code. Read this before writing code. The Rust-specific sections apply
wherever the medium is a Rust crate.

## Line width

Source lines, including doc comments and inline comments, wrap at the source width in prose.md's
[Line widths](prose.md#line-widths), which matches rustfmt's default `max_width`. The per-commit
flow's `cargo fmt` enforces it for code, and the same limit applies to the comment text it doesn't
reflow.

## Comments are prose

Doc comments and inline comments are prose and follow prose.md, its
[Semicolons](prose.md#semicolons) rule included: a commit that edits a source file makes that file's
comment semicolons owed, whole file, code spans and the code itself exempt, and the cycle pays them
in its penultimate rung, or its one commit when single-step, using the prose rule's joins (a period,
a comma with a conjunction, or a restructure). Files outside the cycle's diff are left alone, since
converting them is a sweep and sweeps are their own cycle.

## Doc comments on every file, function, and method

Every `.rs` file must begin with a `//!` module docstring. Every function and method must have a
`///` doc comment. Keep them brief: one sentence of purpose is often enough. The discipline is that
the comment exists, not that it be long. Doc comments follow the [Prose form](prose.md#prose-form)
shape (intro + bullets).

This is a deliberate override of the generic "write no comments" default that applies to inline `//`
comments. Doc comments on the module / item surface are expected, while inline explanatory comments
inside function bodies remain discouraged unless they capture a non-obvious WHY.

**Clap-derive args:** doc comments on `#[arg(...)]` fields drive `--help` output. Clap reflows by
default and collapses bullets into running prose. Add `#[arg(verbatim_doc_comment, ...)]` on any
field whose doc comment uses bullets so each `- ...` lands on its own line in the rendered help.

## `// OK: ...` comments on `unwrap*` calls (Rust)

([why](rationale.md#-ok--comments-on-unwrap-calls-rust))

The default in non-test code is to **not** use `.unwrap()`, `.expect(...)`, or the
`.unwrap_or*(...)` siblings. Prefer a shape that doesn't need them (`match`, `if let`, slice
patterns, infallible-by-construction APIs), which is usually also the clearer code. This is a lean,
not a ban: some sites are legitimately best expressed with one. Two kinds of risk, both in scope:

- `.unwrap()` / `.expect(...)`: a panic path.
- `.unwrap_or(...)` / `.unwrap_or_default()` / `.unwrap_or_else(...)`: no panic, but a silently
  substituted value that can hide a wrong result.

When one is used, three obligations attach:

- A trailing `// OK: ...` comment justifying why the call is acceptable:
  - `// OK: <specific reason>`: document the real precondition, invariant, or domain reason.
    Preferred whenever the reason isn't self-evident.
  - `// OK: obvious`: the default is self-evident from context (e.g.
    `desc.lines().next().unwrap_or("")`, where an empty desc gives an empty title).
  - Bare `// OK` is not used (reads like a truncated comment). Abbreviations (e.g. `SE`) are not
    used because they require a decoder ring for readers seeing the code out of context.
- **Alert the user in conversation** when introducing one, so the site gets reviewed and appropriate
  uses are learned. Don't let it ride in silently on a larger diff.
- For `.unwrap()` / `.expect(...)`, an `#[allow(...)]` at the site when the crate enables the
  project-wide lints in `Cargo.toml`, the recommended base:

  ```toml
  [lints.clippy]
  unwrap_used = "warn"
  expect_used = "warn"
  ```

  Every panicking site is then opt-in and visible in the diff, and clippy (in the per-commit flow)
  catches any that slip through. A crate without the lints owes the comment and the alert alone,
  and the `#[allow]` returns with the lints. The `_or*` siblings have no clippy lint. They are
  covered by the comment convention and the conversational alert. (The template repository's
  `CargoRust.toml` seeds a base `Cargo.toml` with this section already in place.)

```rust
let max = stderr_level.unwrap_or(LevelFilter::Info); // OK: default verbosity when -v/-vv absent
let first_line = desc.lines().next().unwrap_or("");  // OK: obvious

match matches.len() {
    1 => {
        #[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]
        // OK: `1 =>` arm guarantees matches.len() == 1
        Ok(TitleMatch::One(matches.into_iter().next().unwrap()))
    }
    // ...
}
```

Tests (`#[cfg(test)]`) are exempt, since panicking on setup failure is the correct test behavior.

No, nothing in vc-x1 parses a list of file entries with attributes, so there was nothing to reuse for the manifest. I searched `src/` and `xtask/src/` for it.

The closest existing pieces, and why each falls short:

- **`toml_simple`** (`src/toml_simple.rs`): the reader behind `.vc-config.md`. It flattens a file into `key -> string` and has `toml_get_list` for a flat array of strings (used for `validate.fast` and the command lists). It has no notion of an array of tables, so it cannot carry a `kind` or `from` per path.
- **`agent_files::diff::set_files`** (`src/agent_files/diff.rs:217`): today's definition of the set, hard-coded as `AGENTS.md`, the plain files under `agent-data/`, and `custom.md` on request. It lists files but parses nothing. This is what the `agent-files` rung replaces.
- **`xtask_cmd::files`** (`src/xtask_cmd.rs:203`): walks `xtask/` on disk for `xtask copy`; again a directory walk, not a parsed list.
- **`toml_edit`**: already used in `src/xtask_cmd.rs` and `xtask/` to read and edit `Cargo.toml`. `file_set.rs` uses it the same way, so no new dependency.

One design alternative you may be pointing at: the manifest could avoid tables and use three flat lists that `toml_simple` already reads, for example `verbatim = ["AGENTS.md", "agent-data/"]`. That would reuse the existing reader, but `from` would need a separate mapping, which is why I went with `[[file]]`. If you prefer the flat form, say so and I'll rework the rung.

message.content:
Can those functions use this new code, the point is parsing files is a common need and we should create a module
that does this and eventually use it other libraries, thoughts only on that?

content.text:
Yes, they can, and I think it is the right shape, with one adjustment: the shared need is less the TOML parsing than what comes after it.

**What the three callers actually share**

`set_files` and `xtask_cmd::files` parse nothing. Each turns "these paths under this root" into a set of relative file paths; `agent-files diff` and `copy` then compare and copy two roots by that set, and I expect `xtask copy` does the same, though I have not read its copy path closely. `init --from` needs the same things. So the common module has three layers:

1. **Declare**: a list of path entries, each validated as a relative path inside the root. This is what `file_set.rs` has now.
2. **Resolve**: entries against a root into the set of files there, with a directory expanded and a missing file simply absent. This is `set_files` and `xtask_cmd::files` today, written twice.
3. **Compare and copy**: two roots by a resolved set, giving same, differs, only-here, only-there, then the copy. This is `agent_files::diff::compare` and `copy` today.

**How I would shape it**

- **Mechanism in the module, policy in the caller.** The module would own layers 1 to 3. What a kind means (replace, write when absent, only when asked) stays with `init` and `agent-files`, since it is specific to a set.
- **`xtask copy` fits as a caller.** `xtask/` is in effect one verbatim directory entry. Its `Cargo.toml` member wiring and version comparison would stay its own.
- **Keep the module free of the rest of vc-x1.** `file_set.rs` already depends only on `std` and `toml_edit` and returns `String` errors. If that holds, lifting it into a workspace crate later is a move, not a rewrite. That matters if "other libraries" includes `xtask`, which cannot depend on the `vc-x1` binary crate.

**What it means for this cycle**

- **This rung:** stays as it is; nothing in it blocks the wider shape. At most I would rename the kind-specific parts so the generic entry and the set's kinds are visibly separate.
- **`init --from` rung:** adds resolve and copy to the module rather than to `init`.
- **`agent-files` rung:** becomes "`set_files`, `compare` and `copy` move onto the module", which is slightly larger than planned but removes the duplicate rather than adding a third.
- **`xtask copy`:** I would leave it out of this cycle and file it as a Todo, since it is outside the cycle's subject.

One open design point: whether a directory entry means the plain files directly under it (what `set_files` does for `agent-data/`) or everything beneath it (what `xtask/` and `notes/` need). I would make it recursive.

You were right: recursion was only stated in the deliberation and a doc comment, with no code behind it. It is now implemented in this rung. Full validate passed and the dev build is reinstalled.

- **`file_set::resolve`**: turns an entry's path under a root into the files it stands for. A file is itself, a directory is every file beneath it at any depth, and a path that is not there gives nothing.
- **Symlinks** are taken as files and never followed, so the walk stays under the root and cannot loop. This is my choice; say if you want them followed or refused.
- **Test**: `a_directory_is_every_file_beneath_it` covers a file, a three-level directory, a sub-directory, an empty directory and an absent path.
- **Rungs**: this rung's subsection now says the module holds declare and resolve, with recursion spelled out. The `init --from` rung's intent now says the copy runs over the files `resolve` gives, and compare and copy are left to it.

No new `unwrap` sites outside tests. The module is still uncalled, so the `expect(dead_code)` stays until the next rung.

132	### Commit-body form
133	
134	The specimen is [commit-model.md](commit-model.md). A commit body is two plain paragraphs, and the
135	rung's subsection in the record holds the full account, so the breakdown is written once.
136	
137	- **The problem**, and it defines any word the title assumes. It is *this commit's*, never the
138	  cycle's: a body whose problem outruns what the diff resolves is describing something larger than
139	  the commit.
140	- **The solution**, opening "Solution:". No bullets, so a `--body` flag cannot mistake it for an

specimens rather than a skeleton: a work rung's body and a bookend's. Copy the shape, not the

## A work rung

Title: `refactor: split loader from parser`

```
Config loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load a
config without parsing it and a test cannot parse one without a file on
disk. The move into its own module is what forces the split.

Solution: a loader finds and reads the file and a parser takes text and
returns the schema, so a test hands the parser a string, and `main` gets
the schema from one call.

See details in TODO.md:
##### refactor: split loader from parser
```

is the rung's subsection heading, a line of its own, which a search of `TODO.md` finds at any
commit.

```
Opens the cycle "refactor: extract config loader".

See details in TODO.md:
### refactor: extract config loader
```

A bookend resolves no problem of its own, so its body names the cycle by its title and points at
its record, the cycle's heading. The closing's body is the same shape with "Closes".

1	//! Flat plain-struct input to the init op.
2	//!
3	//! `InitParams` is the clap-free shape that `pub fn init` reads
4	//! from. Built `From<&InitArgs>` at the binary edge (main.rs);
5	//! callers without clap (tests, future TUI / library embedding)
6	//! construct it directly.
7	//!
8	//! Per `notes/chores/chores-09.md > ## InitParams implementation
9	//! (0.44.0)`: domain types pass through (`RepoSelector`,
10	//! `ConfigKind`, `PushRetryOptions`); leaf clap wrappers do not.
11	
12	use crate::config::RepoSelector;
13	use crate::init::InitArgs;
14	use crate::options_flags::config::ConfigKind;
15	use crate::options_flags::push_retry::PushRetryOptions;
16	
17	/// Inputs to the init op, flat, owned, clap-free.
18	///
19	/// - `target`: `--target` (URL, path, or
20	///   bare NAME).
21	/// - `name`: optional `--name` override.
22	/// - `account`: `--account` value (None => default account chain).
23	/// - `repo`: `--repo` value parsed into a `RepoSelector`.
24	/// - `test_remotes`: `--test-repo`, the directory its bare remotes,
25	///   named by the repo, go in, in place of the `--repo` chain.
26	/// - `por`: `-s` resolved, `true` for `por`, a plain single repo,
27	///   `false` (default) for dual workspace.
28	/// - `private`: `--private`.
29	/// - `dry_run`: `--dry-run`.
30	/// - `push_retry`: `--push-retries` / `--push-retry-delay`.
31	/// - `config`: resolved `--config` value (None => canned write).
32	/// - `adopt`: `--adopt`, convert an existing target.
33	/// - `upstream`: `--upstream`, the name an adopted test repo's old
34	///   `origin` is kept under, None removing it.
35	/// - `agent_dir`, `agent_repo`, `agent_suffix`: the `--agent-*`
36	///   flags, None meaning the default (dual only).
37	/// - `create_symlink`: whether `init` should create the
38	///   `~/.claude/projects/` symlink for dual runs (production
39	///   path = true; test fixtures suppress with false).
40	pub struct InitParams {
41	    pub target: String,
42	    pub name: Option<String>,
43	    pub account: Option<String>,
44	    pub repo: Option<RepoSelector>,
45	    pub test_remotes: Option<String>,
46	    pub por: bool,
47	    pub private: bool,
48	    pub dry_run: bool,
49	    pub push_retry: PushRetryOptions,
50	    pub config: Option<ConfigKind>,
51	    pub adopt: bool,
52	    pub upstream: Option<String>,
53	    pub no_url_trailer: bool,
54	    pub agent_dir: Option<String>,
55	    pub agent_repo: Option<String>,
56	    pub agent_suffix: Option<String>,
57	    pub create_symlink: bool,
58	}
59	
60	impl From<&InitArgs> for InitParams {
61	    /// Convert clap-derived `InitArgs` into the flat `InitParams`.
62	    ///
63	    /// Production path: sets `create_symlink: true`. Tests that
64	    /// need `create_symlink: false` construct `InitParams`
65	    /// directly (or post-edit the field).
66	    fn from(a: &InitArgs) -> Self {
67	        Self {
68	            // OK: clap requires TARGET unless the retired --target was
69	            // given, and `to_params` refuses that first
70	            target: a.target.clone().unwrap_or_default(),
71	            name: a.name.clone(),
72	            account: a.account.value.clone(),
73	            repo: a.repo.value.clone(),
74	            test_remotes: a.test_repo.clone(),
75	            por: a.por.is_por(),
76	            private: a.provision.private.value,
77	            dry_run: a.provision.dry_run.value,
78	            push_retry: a.provision.push_retry.clone(),
79	            config: a.config.resolve(ConfigKind::None),
80	            adopt: a.adopt,
81	            upstream: a.upstream.clone(),
82	            no_url_trailer: a.no_url_trailer,
83	            agent_dir: a.agent_dir.clone(),
84	            agent_repo: a.agent_repo.clone(),
85	            agent_suffix: a.agent_suffix.clone(),
86	            create_symlink: true,
87	        }
88	    }
89	}
90

28	
29	/// CLI args for `vc-x1 init`.
30	#[derive(Args, Debug)]
31	pub struct InitArgs {
32	    /// What to create: URL, path, or bare NAME, the one positional.
33	    ///
34	    /// - URL: `git@host:owner/name(.git)?`, `https://...(.git)?`,
35	    ///   used as-is, config not consulted.
36	    /// - Path: `./X`, `../X`, `/X`, `~/X`, `~`, `.`, `..`, is the
37	    ///   directory path, remote resolved via `--repo` chain.
38	    /// - Bare NAME: becomes NAME.git, remote resolved via
39	    ///   `--repo` chain.
40	    ///
41	    /// A slashed target with no path prefix (`owner/name`) is
42	    /// refused: it reads equally as a path and as the retired
43	    /// owner/name shorthand, so pass `./owner/name` or a URL.
44	    #[arg(
45	        value_name = "TARGET",
46	        value_hint = ValueHint::AnyPath,
47	        required_unless_present = "target_flag",
48	        verbatim_doc_comment
49	    )]
50	    pub target: Option<String>,
51	
52	    /// Retired: a second positional, the old `TARGET NAME`, refused
53	    /// naming `--name`.
54	    #[arg(value_name = "RETIRED", hide = true, num_args = 0..)]
55	    pub retired: Vec<String>,
56	
57	    /// Retired: `--target`, the target positional now, refused naming it.
58	    #[arg(long = "target", value_name = "TARGET", hide = true)]
59	    pub target_flag: Option<String>,
60	
61	    /// Make the target a throwaway test repo, its bare remotes in
62	    /// REMOTES, so nothing leaves this machine.
63	    ///
64	    /// The remotes are named by the repo, `<name>.git` and
65	    /// `<name>.agent-session.git`, so several test repos share one
66	    /// REMOTES, and a name already there is refused. REMOTES is
67	    /// always a path, so `tmp/remotes` needs no `./`. Not with a URL
68	    /// target, or what names a remote. With `--adopt` the target
69	    /// is an existing repo or directory, an origin it has replaced by
70	    /// REMOTES and kept only by `--upstream`.
71	    #[arg(
72	        long = "test-repo",
73	        value_name = "REMOTES",
74	        value_hint = ValueHint::AnyPath,
75	        verbatim_doc_comment
76	    )]
77	    pub test_repo: Option<String>,
78	
79	    /// Repo directory name override (URL form only).
80	    ///
81	    /// - URL form: repo created at `cwd/<NAME>` instead of the
82	    ///   URL-derived name.
83	    /// - Path / bare-NAME forms: error if given (TARGET already
84	    ///   names the repo).
85	    #[arg(long = "name", value_name = "NAME", verbatim_doc_comment)]
86	    pub name: Option<String>,
87	
88	    /// `--account`: flatten of the shared [`AccountOption`] leaf.
89	    #[command(flatten)]
90	    pub account: AccountOption,
91	
92	    /// `--repo`: flatten of the shared [`RepoOption`] leaf.
93	    /// Init's built-in categories: `remote` (a URL prefix init
94	    /// appends `/<NAME>.git` to) and `local` (parent dir for
95	    /// fixture bare repos). Meaningful only with Path or
96	    /// bare-NAME targets.
97	    #[command(flatten)]
98	    pub repo: RepoOption,
99	
100	    /// `-s/--scope both|por`: flatten of the shared [`PorFlag`]
101	    /// leaf. `both` (default) -> dual workspace (work +
102	    /// `.agent-session/` agent repo), `por` -> plain single repo.
103	    #[command(flatten)]
104	    pub por: PorFlag,
105	
106	    /// `--dry-run` + `--private` + `--push-retries` /
107	    /// `--push-retry-delay`: flatten of the shared
108	    /// [`ProvisionOptionFlagBundle`] bundle.
109	    #[command(flatten)]
110	    pub provision: ProvisionOptionFlagBundle,
111	
112	    /// `--config none|<path>`: flatten of the shared
113	    /// [`ConfigOption`] leaf. Only meaningful with `-s por`,
114	    /// rejected at preflight when paired with the default dual
115	    /// shape. `.gitignore` is always written regardless of
116	    /// `--config`.
117	    #[command(flatten)]
118	    pub config: ConfigOption,
119	
120	    /// Convert an existing TARGET into a dual workspace rather than
121	    /// refuse it.
122	    ///
123	    /// TARGET may be a plain directory, a repo with no workspace
124	    /// config, or a single-repo workspace. A dual workspace is
125	    /// refused, having nothing to grow.
126	    #[arg(long)]
127	    pub adopt: bool,
128	
129	    /// With `--test-repo` and `--adopt`, keep the adopted repo's old
130	    /// `origin` as the remote NAME [default NAME: upstream], where it
131	    /// is otherwise removed.
132	    ///
133	    /// The test repo's remotes are REMOTES either way, and nothing
134	    /// vc-x1 runs pushes to NAME, so it is there to fetch from. A NAME
135	    /// the repo already has is refused.
136	    #[arg(
137	        long,
138	        value_name = "NAME",
139	        num_args = 0..=1,
140	        default_missing_value = "upstream",
141	        requires_all = ["test_repo", "adopt"],
142	        verbatim_doc_comment
143	    )]
144	    pub upstream: Option<String>,
145	
146	    /// Stamp each initial commit's `ochid:` alone, with no `orepo:` link.
147	    /// A plain repo stamps no trailer, so it changes nothing there.
148	    #[arg(long)]
149	    pub no_url_trailer: bool,
150	
151	    /// The agent repo's directory, one name inside the project
152	    /// directory [default: .agent-session]. Dual only.
153	    #[arg(long, value_name = "DIR", value_parser = parse_agent_dir)]
154	    pub agent_dir: Option<String>,
155	
156	    /// The agent repo's full name on its remote. Dual only.
157	    ///
158	    /// Default: the work repo's name plus `--agent-suffix`.
159	    #[arg(long, value_name = "NAME", conflicts_with = "agent_suffix")]
160	    pub agent_repo: Option<String>,
161	
162	    /// The suffix the work repo's name takes to name the agent
163	    /// repo on its remote, beginning with `.` or `-`
164	    /// [default: .agent-session]. Dual only.
165	    #[arg(
166	        long,
167	        value_name = "SUFFIX",
168	        allow_hyphen_values = true,
169	        value_parser = parse_agent_suffix
170	    )]
171	    pub agent_suffix: Option<String>,
172	}
173	
174	/// Parse `--agent-dir`: one name inside the project directory.
175	///
176	/// One name, not a path, since the agent side's own config reaches
177	/// the work repo as `..`. `.git` and `.jj` are the work repo's own.

input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='TODO.md'
s=open(p).read()
old='''The copy is `file_set`'s, over the files `resolve` gives, a directory entry taken at every depth,
and what each kind does with them is `init`'s.
'''
new=old+'''
- The mechanism is `file_set`'s: `files_of` pairs each file of an entry with where a copy writes
  it, a directory's files beneath the entry's path wherever a `from` reads them, and `copy_file`
  copies one, told whether a different file there is replaced or kept, given a fill for the text,
  and keeping the source's permissions, so a script stays one.
- The policy is `init`'s, `src/init/set.rs`: verbatim is replaced with no fill, a starter is
  written only when absent with `{name}` filled by the directory's name, and an optional entry is
  left out, or with `--custom` written as a starter is, so a `custom.md` there is never replaced.
- The copy is a step of its own, after the config and `init`'s `TODO.md` and `zTOC.md`, before the
  first commit, so the set is in that commit, a starter of a name `init` writes is kept out, and
  the dry run prints the step with the set and its manifest.
- The preflight refuses, with nothing made, a source that is no directory or is the target, a
  manifest that does not parse, and an entry the copy takes that has no file in the source, since
  a set listing what it lacks would make a workspace missing it. `resolve` itself stays lenient,
  for a diff of two copies.
- A verbatim file only in the destination is left there. `init` deletes nothing, and the delete
  `agent-files copy` does is the next rung's.
- The flags are `-s por`'s as much as a dual workspace's, a plain repo taking a set the same way.
- The source is read as its working copy holds it, with no `--landed` yet, the script's reading of
  a revision by `git archive`.
- Open, for the review: the script also gives the work `.gitignore` the lines `/tmp`,
  `/tmp-durable`, and `/custom.md`, which no manifest entry says. Without them `--custom` puts
  `custom.md` in the first commit, where it is meant to be local.
'''
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
set -o pipefail; cargo xtask validate 2>&1 | tee tmp/last.log | tail -4

The rung **feat: init --from copies a set by its manifest** is written and ready for review. Full validate passed, and `vc-x1-dev` is `0.85.29-2` from the working copy.

**What changed**
- **`file_set`**: gains `files_of` (each file of an entry paired with where it is written) and `copy_file` (copy one file, told whether to replace or keep a different one, with an optional text fill, keeping the source's permissions). The `expect(dead_code)` is gone.
- **`src/init/set.rs`** (new): the flags `--from <SOURCE>`, `--file-set <PATH>` and `--custom`, the preflight, and the copy step.
  - Verbatim files are replaced.
  - Starters are written only when absent, with `{name}` filled.
  - Optional entries are written only with `--custom`, and then as a starter is.
- **`init`**: the copy is its own step, after the config and `init`'s own `TODO.md` and `zTOC.md`, before the first commit. It runs for `-s por` too.
- **Preflight** refuses, with nothing made:
  - a source that is not a directory, or is the target itself;
  - a manifest that does not parse;
  - an entry the copy takes that has no file in the source.

**Tried with the dev build** in a scratch home, `init ./hello --test-repo ./remotes --from <vc-x1>`:
- The dry run lists the copy as step 3 of 11.
- The real run reported 23 written, 0 replaced, 2 kept (`TODO.md` and `zTOC.md`, `init`'s own).
- `agent-files diff --from <vc-x1>` in the new workspace reports 0 of 15 differ.
- `README.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` have `hello` filled in, there is no `custom.md`, and the working copy is clean after the first commit.

**Decision for you**
- **`.gitignore` lines:** `vc-dr-apply.sh` also adds `/tmp`, `/tmp-durable` and `/custom.md` to the work `.gitignore`, and no manifest entry says that. Without them, `--custom` puts `custom.md` into the first commit, where it is meant to be local. I recommend a `gitignore = [...]` list in `file-set.toml` that `init` merges the way it already merges its own lines; the alternative is leaving it to a later cycle. It is recorded as open in the rung's subsection.

**Also worth knowing**
- `init` deletes nothing: a verbatim file that exists only in the destination stays. The delete that `agent-files copy` does is left to the next rung.
- The source is read from its working copy; there is no `--landed` equivalent yet.
- No new `unwrap` or `expect` sites outside tests.

Yes, now you can: the dry run of `init --from` prints the list. There was no way to see it before, so I added it to this rung; full validate passed and `vc-x1-dev` has it.

Run this from the vc-x1 root (the target is not created, any unused path works):

```
vc-x1-dev init ~/tmp/see-list --test-repo ~/tmp/see-remotes --from . --dry-run
```

After the eleven steps it prints one line per file: its kind, where it is written, and where it is read when that differs. For vc-x1's own set that is 25 files:

- **verbatim (15):** `AGENTS.md` and the 14 files under `agent-data/`.
- **starter (10):** `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `README.md`, `TODO.md`, `zTOC.md` and the four `notes/` files, each read from `scripts/vc-dr-apply-base/work/`, plus `LICENSE-APACHE` and `LICENSE-MIT` read from their own paths.

Add `--custom` to see `custom.md` join the list as `optional`.

Two limits of the list as it stands:
- It shows what the set holds, not what a real run would do to each file. `TODO.md` and `zTOC.md` appear as starters, but `init` writes its own first, so the set's are skipped.
- It only exists under `init --dry-run`. There is no standalone command to list a set; say if you want one.

The `.gitignore` lines decision from my last message is still open.

The `gitignore` list is in `file-set.toml`, and `init --from` now applies it. Full validate passed and `vc-x1-dev` has it.

- **Manifest:** `file-set.toml` gains `gitignore = ["/tmp", "/tmp-durable", "/custom.md"]` before the entries, the same lines the script's `gitignore-lines` holds. The parser accepts it as a list of one-line strings and refuses a non-list, a non-string, an empty line or a duplicate.
- **Copy step:** after the files, `init` adds each line the work `.gitignore` lacks, so `custom.md` is ignored before the first commit.
- **Dry run:** now also prints the lines it would add, after the file list.
- **Refactor:** the line-adding is `file_set::add_lines`, and `init`'s existing merge of its own two lines (the agent directory and `.claude/settings.local.json`) now goes through it too.

Tried with the dev build in the scratch home, `init ./hello2 --test-repo ./remotes --from <vc-x1> -c`: the new `.gitignore` ends with `/tmp`, `/tmp-durable`, `/custom.md`, and `custom.md` is not in the first commit.

content.text:
The rung **feat: agent-files copy and diff read the manifest** is written and ready for review. Full validate passed, and `vc-x1-dev` is `0.85.29-3` from the working copy.

**What changed**
- **The set is read from the manifest.** `agent-files diff` and `copy` take the source's `file-set.toml`: its verbatim entries, plus its optional ones with `-c`. Each command now prints which list it read.
- **Fallbacks:**
  - A source with no manifest uses the built-in set as before (`AGENTS.md`, `agent-data/`, `custom.md` on request), so older copies still diff.
  - A manifest that does not parse is an error, never a silent fallback.
- **`file_set` gains the third layer:** `compare` (how the files under a list of paths differ between two roots) and `covers` (whether a path is in the list, used by the copy's dirty-working-copy guard). `set_files` and `in_set` are gone, and `copy` now copies through `file_set::copy_file`.
- **`from` is `init`'s only.** `diff` and `copy` read each path at itself on both sides, so `agent-files copy -c` still copies the adopter's own `custom.md`. That settles the open point from the first rung.
- **Starters are never compared or copied**, as before.
- **`agent-data/` is now taken at every depth.** It holds no subdirectory today, so nothing changes for the set as it is.

**Tried with the dev build**, against the scratch workspace `init --from` made earlier:
- `agent-files copy --from <vc-x1>` reports the set by vc-x1's `file-set.toml` and "already the same, nothing to do".
- `agent-files diff` with the scratch workspace as `--from` reports the built-in set and 0 of 15 differ.

**Decision for you**
- **A workspace made by `init --from` is not itself a set.** It holds no `file-set.toml` and none of the starter templates under `scripts/vc-dr-apply-base/`, so it cannot be the `--from` of another `init`, and `diff` from it falls back to the built-in list (seen in the second trial). That sits oddly with "an adopter carries a copy of the set". Making the manifest and the templates part of what is copied would fix it, but it changes what the set is, so I have not done it. I can add it as a rung, or file it as a Todo.

**Left out**
- `agent-files size` still lists the set with its own code; its table columns are bound to those file names. The existing Todo **feat: agent-files-size should exclude custom.md** is where it gets reworked.

No new `unwrap` or `expect` sites outside tests.

please review

content.text:
Your surprise is justified, and it points at a real inconsistency in what I built: the two commands read `custom.md` from different places.

- **`init --from ... --custom`** wrote the new workspace's `custom.md` from the skeleton template, `scripts/vc-dr-apply-base/work/custom.md`. That is what the `from` on the `custom.md` entry in `file-set.toml` tells it to do. The template is a ten-line stub: a heading, a paragraph, and an empty "Local permissions and overrides" section.
- **`agent-files diff -c`** compares the file at its own path on both sides, so it compared that stub against vc-x1's real `custom.md`, with its long-output commands, messaging rules and the agent-files draft note.

So the diff is correct about the bytes, and they differ a lot because one is a blank starter and the other is vc-x1's local layer. Both behaviours were deliberate, but together `-c` means two different things, which is the surprise.

**The decision is which `custom.md` a new workspace should get with `-c`:**

1. **The stub (today).** A new workspace starts with an empty local layer, as `vc-dr-apply.sh` does. `diff -c` against the source will always show `custom.md` as differing, and `agent-files copy -c` would then overwrite the stub with the source's.
2. **The source's own `custom.md`.** Drop the `from` on that entry, so `init -c` copies what `copy -c` copies and `diff -c` reports "same". The cost is that the new workspace inherits the source's machine-local notes (vc-x1's messaging permission, for example), which may not apply to it.

I recommend option 1 for `init`, but making it less surprising. Two ways to do that:

- always write the stub and drop `-c` from `init`, since a stub carries nothing private and every workspace needs one to exist (it is gitignored either way); or
- keep `-c` and have `diff` say "project layer" rather than "differs" for it.

My preference is the first: a new workspace's `custom.md` is a starter, not an optional copy of someone else's local file. That would make the `custom.md` entry a starter in the manifest, with `optional` then meaning only "the source's own file, on request" for `agent-files copy` and `diff`.

**On your question:** `vc-x1-dev init ./xxx -c` with no `--from` is refused by the argument parser before anything runs:

```
error: the following required arguments were not provided:
  --from <SOURCE>
```

That was already the behaviour and I left it, since without a source there is no `custom.md` to take.

**What changed**
- **Manifest:** the `custom.md` entry in `file-set.toml` no longer has a `from`, so it is read from the source's own path.
- **`init`:** an optional file is written as the source holds it, with no `{name}` fill, and only when the target has none.
- **Source without `custom.md`:** `init --from <SOURCE> -c` is refused in the preflight with nothing made, the same as any listed file the source lacks.
- **Test:** the test of vc-x1's own manifest no longer requires optional files to exist in the tree, because `custom.md` is gitignored and absent from a clone.

One consequence to be aware of: a workspace made with `-c` inherits vc-x1's local notes as they are (the messaging permission and the stale `v0.3.1-13` draft line included). Without `-c` a new workspace gets no `custom.md` at all, since the stub template is no longer used by anything in the manifest.

The earlier open decision still stands: a workspace made by `init --from` holds no `file-set.toml` or starter templates, so it cannot itself be a `--from` source.

The rung **fix: init refuses a taken symlink path up front** is written and ready for review. Full validate passed, and `vc-x1-dev` is `0.85.29-4` from the working copy.

**What changed**
- **`symlink::check`** (new): works out the `~/.claude/projects/<mangled-path>` path `init` would link, and refuses if something that is not a symlink is already there. A symlink there, wherever it points, is left for the existing install step to keep or replace.
- **`init` preflight:** calls the check before anything is made, and only when `init` would create the symlink (a dual workspace from the command line). `-s por` and the test fixtures make no symlink, so they are not checked.
- **The refusal** names the path, says a Claude Code session started in the directory made it, and gives the `mv <path> <path>.before-init` command that clears it. `init` moves nothing itself.

**Tried with the dev build** in the scratch home: with a real directory at the symlink path, `init ./sess --test-repo ./remotes` exits 1 during "Preflight checks...", and neither `sess` nor `remotes/sess.git` was created.

**To consider in the review**
- The error is long, because the mangled path appears three times (the path, then twice in the `mv` command). I can shorten it by printing the path once and writing the `mv` with a placeholder; say if you want that.
- `clone` installs the same symlink as its last step and does not get this check here; I left it out as outside the rung and recorded it in the subsection.

No new `unwrap` or `expect` sites outside tests.

please review

The rung **fix: init adopts a .claude-only directory** is written and ready for review. Full validate passed, and `vc-x1-dev` is `0.85.29-5` from the working copy.

**What changed**
- **A directory holding only `.claude/` is adopted without `--adopt`.** That is what a Claude Code session started in an empty directory leaves behind. A directory with anything else in it still needs the flag.
- **An adopted plain directory's `.claude/` is ignored.** When the target is a plain directory holding `.claude/`, `init` adds `/.claude` to the work `.gitignore`, so none of it is in the first commit and all of it stays on disk.
- **Unchanged cases:**
  - A fresh workspace still ignores only `/.claude/settings.local.json`.
  - An adopted repo keeps whatever its own history does with `.claude/`.
  - `-s por`, which takes no `--adopt`, does not take a `.claude`-only directory either.
- **Dry run:** the header reads "adopting" and the config step ends "its .claude/ ignored".

**Tried with the dev build** in the scratch home: `init ./claudeonly --test-repo ./remotes --from <vc-x1>` on a directory holding only `.claude/.cc-writes/a` succeeded with no flag. The `.gitignore` has `/.claude` followed by the set's three lines, and zero `.claude` files are in the first commit.

- With the previous rung, a real session directory is refused first for its symlink path; once that is moved aside, `init <TARGET>` works with no flag. Your hand test with `../hello` is the end-to-end check of that, since my sandbox cannot start a real session.
- The wider rule, **Every repo's .gitignore ignores .claude, and settings stay out of agent-repos**, stays a Todo; this rung only covers the adopted directory.

content.text:
It is valid Markdown. That text was already in vc-x1's own `custom.md` before this cycle, and `init -c` now copies the file as it is.

The link in `custom.md` lines 14-15 is:

```
- Long output: the commands this workspace adds to [Working
  practices](AGENTS.md#working-practices)' Long output rule, ...
```

CommonMark allows a line break inside a link's text (the part in `[...]`); it renders as a space, so the link reads "Working practices". What may not be split is the `](` join or the destination in `(...)`, and neither is here. The agent-files wrap link text the same way in many places, for example `[The In Progress\nblock](agent-data/notes.md#the-in-progress-block)` in `TODO.md`.

Two caveats:

- **Some previewers handle it less well than the spec.** If it looks broken in your viewer, that is the viewer, but it is still a reason to keep a link on one line where it fits.
- **The checker did not verify this link.** `vc-x1-dev check anchors --file custom.md` reports "0 link(s) checked, 0 failed, 2 cross-file skipped". The `AGENTS.md#working-practices` target does exist, but cross-file links are skipped; that gap is already a Todo (**validate-anchors resolves a cross-file link**).

If you would rather have it unsplit, I can rejoin it in `custom.md`. That file is gitignored and local, so it would not be part of this rung's commit.

content.text:
I think the rule is a good one, but it is an agent-files change and a 128-link sweep, so I would not fold it into this rung. I have changed nothing yet.

**Why I like it**
- **Searchable:** a link kept on one line can be found by its text; a wrapped `[Working\n  practices]` cannot.
- **Renders everywhere:** it removes the dependence on how a previewer treats a break inside link text.
- **Checkable:** "no link spans a line" is easy for `check anchors` to enforce, and it would let the wrapped-citation bug (**validate-anchors finds a citation that follows a wrapped code span**) be closed by rule rather than by parser work.

**The cost**
- **Ragged lines:** a line that breaks early before a link will look short. I think that is a fair trade.
- **The sweep:** 128 links currently wrap across a line, in these places:

| Where | Wrapped links |
|---|---|
| Agent-files (`AGENTS.md`, `agent-data/*`) | 65 |
| `TODO.md` | 32 |
| `notes/` | 16 |
| `README.md` | 11 |
| The skeleton templates | 2 |
| `zTOC.md` | 1 |
| `custom.md` | 1 |

**How I would word the rule** (in `prose.md > Line widths`):
- A link, text and destination, is never split across lines.
- If it does not fit on the current line within 100 columns, it starts the next line.
- A link longer than 100 columns on its own is the exception to the width, as a URL already is.

One reading to confirm: after a link that moved to the next line, I would let the following text continue on that same line when it fits, and only push it to the line after when the link itself fills the line. Your "by itself" could instead mean the link always sits alone on its line; that would be simpler to check but more ragged.

**Where it should go**
- **`custom.md`:** local and gitignored, one link. I can fix it now, outside any commit.
- **The rule and the agent-files sweep:** the next cycle, **agent-files(proposal): v0.3.1**, since changing `prose.md` is an agent-files change with its own version bump.
- **The checker and the remaining files:** either rungs of that cycle or a Todo of their own. The agent-files say a sweep is its own cycle, and prose elsewhere converts when a cycle touches the file.

If you agree, I'll fix `custom.md` now and add a Todo entry for the rule, the check and the sweep. Or say if you want it as a rung of this cycle instead.

- **The short lines are a fair trade** (wink, 2026-11-25): a line broken early before a link is
  ragged in the source alone, never rendered.
- **What follows a moved link**, open: the agent reads the rule as letting the text after a link
  go on along its line while it fits, the line after taking it only when the link fills its own.
  Wink's "on the next line by itself" may mean a moved link is always alone on its line.
- **The sweep**: the agent-files by the cycle that makes the rule, `TODO.md` (32), `notes/` (16),
  `README.md` (11), and the skeleton's templates (2) as a cycle touches each or by a sweep of its
  own, as the semicolons went. `custom.md`'s one was joined by hand, the file being local.
- Closes **validate-anchors finds a citation that follows a wrapped code span** by rule.
- To be carried by **agent-files(proposal): v0.3.1**.

'''
open(p,'w').write(s.replace(anchor,entry+anchor))
EOF

input.command:
set -o pipefail; vc-x1-dev rung commit -s b --body "A Claude Code session started in a directory leaves a .claude/ there.
init then refuses the directory as existing unless --adopt is given, and
adopting it commits the session's files, since the work .gitignore
ignores only the settings file under .claude/.

Solution: a directory holding .claude/ and nothing else is adopted with
no flag, taken as the empty directory it otherwise is, and one holding
more still needs --adopt. A plain directory adopted with a .claude/ gets
/.claude in the work .gitignore, so none of it is in the first commit
and all of it stays on disk. A fresh workspace and an adopted repo are
unchanged.

See details in TODO.md:
##### fix: init adopts a .claude-only directory" 2>&1 | tee tmp/last.log | tail -25
